name: fsdiag
description: Filesystem diagnostics: why are my tunnels slow? Times file system calls on the login node and on compute nodes (any, or the ones you name), counts what your folders hold and reads your quotas, and says what the REST server's slow requests were waiting for. Runs on the login node as you.

fsdiag.title: Filesystem diagnostics
fsdiag.description: Finds out why tunnel requests are slow: per-call file system latency on the login node and on compute nodes, how many files your folders hold and your quota, and what slow requests were waiting for. It runs on the login node as you; compute-node probes are short SLURM jobs. Only the console's Open (which carries its token) gets in.

settings.name: FSDIAG_PATHS
settings.label: Places to time
settings.hint: colon-separated, LABEL=PATH or PATH; empty: your home, hpclib's data directory, scratch, /tmp and /dev/shm where they exist

settings.name: FSDIAG_PARTITION
settings.label: Partition
settings.hint: for the compute-node probes; empty: the cluster's default

settings.name: FSDIAG_ACCOUNT
settings.label: Account
settings.hint: for the compute-node probes; empty: your default

settings.name: FSDIAG_PYTHON
settings.label: Python
settings.hint: Python 3.6 or newer on the login node; default python3

settings.name: FSDIAG_COMPUTE_PYTHON
settings.label: Python on compute nodes
settings.hint: Python 3.6 or newer there; default python3
